territorial_scope.description: Issued as national measures applying to work units and S&T activities, with provincial-level and industry oversight departments implementing them locally.

evidence.quote: the term “local” refers to the provincial-level administrative department

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health
agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: China's trial Measures require science and technology ethics reviews for S&T activities involving humans, laboratory animals, or other ethically risky activities. Work units set up ethics committees, and listed high-risk activities also need expert reconsideration and registration. Effective 1 December 2023.
summary.long: The Measures apply to S&T activities involving human research participants, laboratory animals, or other activities that may pose ethical risks to life, health, the environment, public order or sustainable development (Art. 2). Work units in life sciences, medicine and artificial intelligence whose research involves sensitive ethics areas must establish S&T ethics (review) committees, which must have at least seven members and must be independent (Arts. 4, 7). Applicants submit materials including risk assessments and informed consent forms (Art. 9). Committees decide to approve, approve with modifications, re-review or disapprove, with a two-thirds majority of members present (Art. 16), generally within 30 days (Art. 17). Simplified procedures apply to minimal-risk activities (Art. 22). Activities on a checklist published by MOST require a preliminary committee review and then expert reconsideration by an oversight department panel (Arts. 25-30). Follow-up reviews occur at intervals of 12 months, or six months for checklist activities (Arts. 19, 33). Committees and work units must register with a national platform within 30 days and file annual reports by 31 March (Arts. 43-45). Penalties for violations are imposed by the competent agency, with civil and criminal liability where applicable, without fixed amounts in this text (Arts. 47-48). The appendix lists checklist activities including algorithmic models that can mobilize public opinion and highly autonomous automated decision-making systems (Appendix).

notes: Relations are limited to the two instruments named in Article 1; generic references to laws, administrative regulations, the Constitution and personal information rules (e.g., Arts. 3, 15, 47, 54) are not coded as relations. target_instrument_id is left empty because neither target is in the registry. The title carries '(Trial)'; Article 56 states implementation from December 1, 2023. Article 30 requires two-thirds 'of all reconsideration experts' while Article 16 requires two-thirds 'of the members present'; these are different voting bases as written, not a contradiction. Article 52 states that periods are natural days unless working days are indicated.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier, prohibition, benefit, penalty or price was found. Numbers present are procedural time limits (Arts 17, 19, 31, 33, 36, 43-45; events), committee and panel size or quorum (Arts 7, 14, 23, 28), and two-thirds voting rules (Arts 16, 30), treated as procedural or composition rules rather than thresholds. Scope is set by qualitative criteria such as 'minimal risks' (Art. 22, Art. 52) and by the Appendix list, which has no numbers.
